content: It includes information on study designs, treatment arms, dosages, durations, and outcomes, as well as quality assessments using the GRADE system. The GRADE system evaluates the quality of evidence and the strength of recommendations based on factors such as risk of bias, consistency, precision, and sample size. The dataset outlines numerous studies, each identified by a name, year, and registration number, and provides details on the medications used (e.g., daclatasvir, sofosbuvir, ledipasvir, asunaprevir, etc.), their dosages, and the duration of treatment. It also specifies whether the studies were observational or interventional and whether the outcomes were considered critical based on the GRADE criteria. The evidence is categorized by patient populations, such as treatment-naïve or treatment-experienced, and by genotype of the condition being treated. The GRADE system is used to assess the quality of evidence, with ratings ranging from very low (⨁) to high (⨁⨁⨁⨁). Factors that may lead to downgrading the quality of evidence include a high risk of bias, inconsistency in results, imprecision due to small sample sizes or wide confidence intervals, and reliance on observational studies. The text also includes a legend explaining the criteria for downgrading evidence quality. In summary, this document is a comprehensive compilation of clinical trial data and evidence assessments for various treatment regimens, providing a detailed overview of their efficacy, safety, and quality of evidence. It is intended for use by medical professionals and researchers to guide treatment decisions and evaluate the strength of the evidence supporting different therapeutic approaches.
